episodes.214800: Monsoon thunderstorms rolled southeast off the Sangre de Cristo Mountains during the late afternoon and evening hours of August 7th over east-central NM. Several of these thunderstorms produced severe wind gusts of 58 to 72 mph in an area from near Tucumcari to Ft. Sumner to Santa Rosa, NM. While no severe wind gust damage was reported in these areas, minor damage was reported from sub-severe thunderstorm wind gusts in Roswell, NM.
episodes.214810: A complex of showers and isolated thunderstorms tracked across western Pennsylvania during the early morning hours and continued to move eastward across central Pennsylvania during the late morning hours. As this complex moved eastward, surface heating ahead of the complex along with increasing moisture and shear allowed for more cohesive development into a line of strong-to-severe thunderstorms as it moved into York and Lancaster Counties. This produced multiple instances of tree damage across Lancaster County with an isolated instance of tree damage in York County. Heavy rainfall later in the evening across northwestern Pennsylvania also brought an isolated instance of flash flooding to Warren County.

episodes.214842: Abnormally dry and hot conditions with limited monsoonal moisture allowed for mostly dry virga showers and isolated thunderstorms to develop over the western and northern mountains of New Mexico August 8th and 9th moving into nearby lower elevations. One virga shower produced a dry microburst over the Raton Crews Municipal Airport on August 8th and a nearby thunderstorm produced a 59 mph wind gust at the Clayton Municipal Airport on August 9th.
episodes.214961: Scattered thunderstorms impacted Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours of August 7, 2026. These thunderstorms produced damaging winds and heavy rain, particularly across Rutherford and Williamson counties. A few trees were reported down, and roadways were flooded and closed.
episodes.214962: An active summertime pattern continued for Middle Tennessee on August 8, 2026, as numerous thunderstorms developed over the area through the late evening hours. These thunderstorms produced very heavy rain, especially in the Williamson County area. Numerous roadways were reported and impassable with home evacuations and water rescues reported in the Franklin area.

episodes.216032: A hot and humid air mass combined with strong northwest winds aloft, to bring a bout of severe storms to eastern Iowa August 7th. Several severe thunderstorms moved across eastern IA between 4pm and 10pm August 7th. Significant wind damage was surveyed in Buchanan and Linn counties with damage to crops, trees, power lines, farm buildings, and damage to siding on homes. The town of Prairieburg and rural portions of Buchanan county received the most extensive damage. In addition, three tornadoes were confirmed near Fairbank, Prairieburg and Rubio.
episodes.216234: Primarily diurnally driven showers and thunderstorms continued to impact the area from August 7th to the 9th under the guise of a front approaching from the northwest and then stalling across Ohio and Pennsylvania. This resulted in the daily formation of afternoon showers and thunderstorms, which produced damaging winds that brought down trees and power lines across southeast Ohio. Given saturated ground from previous rounds of rain already that month, one to three inches of rain produced by heavy downpours in these storms was enough to cause flash flooding on several roads in Meigs County.
episodes.216235: The active weather pattern that began the month of August continued to roll on into the 7th and 8th across West Virginia. This was due to a frontal boundary approaching from the northwest that then stalled across Ohio and Pennsylvania. This primed the atmosphere with ample moisture and unseasonably hot temperatures to help spawn the daily formation of afternoon showers and thunderstorms across the state. Scattered convection that developed both on the 7th and 8th of August inflicted downed trees and power lines across of variety of locations in West Virginia due to the damaging winds associated with the storms. Given the saturated ground from previous rounds of rain, one to three inches of rain produced by heavy downpours in these storms was also enough to cause flash flooding on several roads in West Virginia. Activity remained strongly connected to the warm temperature spread, with the loss of daytime heating at sunset causing their demise each evening.
episodes.216381: On August 8th, troughing over the area triggered early morning convection over the coastal Atlantic waters shifting inland with the Atlantic sea breeze. A daily record precipitable water amount of 2.41 inches was measured on KJAX 12Z sounding. Given abundant moisture and low level convergence, showers and storms quickly spread further inland with stronger storms developing along colliding mesoscale boundaries.
episodes.216469: A weak boundary along the southern Appalachians tied to a trough of low pressure over the Ohio Valley produced isolated to scattered showers and storms in the late afternoon and early evening hours over the Piedmont and Triangle of central North Carolina. Several damaging wind reports were observed in Randolph and Durham Counties.
episodes.216686: Another round of monsoon storms brought some severe weather and heavy rains that led to flash flooding.
episodes.216687: More afternoon monsoon thunderstorms led to some severe weather and flash flooding from heavy rain.
episodes.216710: During the afternoon and evening hours of August 8, 2026, thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts and large hail across portions of eastern Nebraska. The convection moved into the region in association with a mesoscale convective vortex (MCV) and was aided by gravity wave interactions. An initial report of 1.00-inch hail was recorded 2 miles east of Columbus at 11:25 AM CST.||As the complex continued eastward, wind gusts of 73 mph and 65 mph were measured near Leigh, NE, shortly after noon. These severe winds were driven by evaporative cooling from anvil precipitation, which mixed stronger momentum from aloft down to the surface. Later into the evening, a strengthening low-level jet nosing into the region sparked additional thunderstorm development. This secondary activity resulted in another report of 1.00-inch hail in Wisner, NE, at 4:28 PM CST.
episodes.216781: A hot and humid air mass combined with strong northwest winds aloft, to bring a bout of severe storms to eastern Iowa August 7th. Several severe thunderstorms moved across eastern IA between 4pm and 10pm August 7th. Significant wind damage was surveyed in Buchanan and Linn counties with damage to crops, trees, power lines, farm buildings, and damage to siding on homes. The town of Prairieburg and rural portions of Buchanan county received the most extensive damage. In addition, three tornadoes were confirmed near Fairbank, Prairieburg and Rubio.
episodes.217240: A disturbance moved through the region, bringing showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening. Modest instability and weak wind shear supported scattered storms, with a few becoming strong to severe. Storms produced strong wind gusts and hail.
episodes.217273: A cold front passing over Lake Superior on the 7th caused thunderstorms that drove wind gusts as high as 45 mph.
episodes.217355: On August 8th, 2026, a cold front approached from the northwest and slowly passed through the region. Ahead of the front, MLCAPE values exceeded 2000 J/kg, DCAPE of around 1200 J/kg, and low level lapse rates were ranging from 7-8 C/km. Though, shear in the environment was on the low end around 20-25 knots of bulk shear, and with the approaching front, it provided enough lift for isolated severe thunderstorms to develop.
episodes.217448: After a morning round of storms on August 8th, a lull in activity allowed for the development of an unstable atmosphere ahead of an afternoon shortwave. 1500-2000 J/kg of surface-based CAPE, along with around 1000 J/kg of downdraft CAPE, provided the ingredients for some isolated damaging wind gusts as scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms moved across the region.
episodes.217637: A long-lived diurnal thunderstorm produced strong wind gusts and a report of large hail across southern Oklahoma on the evening of the 8th.
episodes.217668: A decaying MCV colocated with a shortwave began rotating into the Mid-South on the morning of August 8th. As peak heating occured, a few thunderstorms began to pop-up with around 1500 J/kg of MUCAPE present, weak laspe rates of around 6 C/km, and PWATs nearing the 90th percentile for this time of the year. Thunderstorms were able to train over West Tennessee resulting in a few impassable roadways.
episodes.217707: Common daytime heating and sea breeze influences resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms, as well as isolated strong to severe storms. Precipitable water values around 2.2+ inches and slow storm motion also resulted in multiple instances of very heavy rainfall and localized flooding.
episodes.217719: A surface boundary moved through Cheyenne County in CO in the afternoon, spawning small thunderstorms. Multiple wind reports from 58-68 mph where recorded near the town of Cheyenne Wells. Two damage reports were also recieved. One report was a pictured healthy large pine tree being snapped in half, the other of multiple storage units being flipped.
episodes.217722: A broad sub-tropical mid to upper level ridge axis was positioned to the east of the area.  A surface high was centered directly over the area with light winds in place.  A sea-breeze boundary developed and pushed inland during the late morning and early afternoon hours as temperatures warmed into the 90s.  An isolated afternoon thunderstorm developed along the sea-breeze boundary in northern Terrebonne Parish and produced localized damaging wind gusts.
episodes.217890: During the late night of the 6th into the early AM hours of the 7th, a complex of storms moved from north to south through the combined OK/TX Panhandles, entering the OK Panhandle first. As this complex moved through it produced thunderstorm winds damage in the OK Panhandle with winds continuing to be measured well above 60 mph by ground stations throughout the area. One isolated updraft produced hail up to the size of nickels near Boise City, OK. After the thunderstorm stopped, decaying showers continued to bring strong winds to the surface from aloft and strong winds continued to be measured by ground stations.
episodes.217896: Scattered storms moved across central Virginia on August 7. These storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.217942: An inverted trough rounding the western periphery of high pressure centered across the Atlantic encountered deep moisture and modest instability supportive of localized heavy rainfall.
episodes.217944: An inverted trough rounding the western periphery of high pressure centered across the Atlantic along with lines of towering cumulus within light wind fields across coastal waters supported showers and thunderstorms capable of producing waterspouts.
episodes.217945: An inverted trough rounding the western periphery of high pressure centered across the Atlantic along with lines of towering cumulus within light wind fields across coastal waters supported showers and thunderstorms capable of producing waterspouts shifting onshore.
episodes.217958: Between August 7 and 9, a weakness emerged along the eastern periphery of a prominent mid-level ridge centered over New Mexico. This atmospheric feature prompted the formation of isolated to scattered thunderstorms across North Texas. A select number of these storms produced localized wind damage and small hail.
episodes.218109: Hot and humid conditions were in place across southern Litchfield County on August 6-7, 2026. Heat index values reached between 95 and 100 degrees each afternoon. In addition, a complex of thunderstorms crossed southern Litchfield County during the early evening hours on August 7 resulting in some incidents of wind damage as well as localized flash flooding, mainly within the Town of Watertown.
episodes.218111: Warm and humid conditions continued across eastern New York on August 8, 2026 well ahead of an approaching cold front. Enough instability and forcing was in place to generate scattered showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon hours. Some of these became severe downing some trees and wires.
episodes.218112: Warm and humid conditions continued across western Massachusetts on August 8, 2026 well ahead of an approaching cold front. Enough instability and forcing was in place to generate scattered showers and thunderstorms during the late afternoon hours. Some of these became severe downing some trees and wires.
episodes.218151: On August 8th, 2026, the Storm Prediction Center placed portions of upstate and central New York under a Marginal to localized Slight Risk as a low-amplitude mid-level shortwave trough tracked eastward through an unstable air mass. Area Forecast Discussions from NWS Buffalo highlighted that daytime surface heating coupled with high humidity produced pockets of moderate MLCAPE exceeding 1,500 to 2,000 J/kg ahead of the boundary. Stronger localized convective cores initiated during the mid-to-late afternoon, progressing across the Eastern Lake America region and Saint Lawrence basin where Special Marine and Severe Thunderstorm Warnings were issued. As storms organized along these outflow and lake breeze boundaries, the primary severe hazards observed were localized damaging wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph and isolated quarter-sized hail before activity shifted eastward.
episodes.218166: During the early afternoon on August 8th, a nearly stationary band of thunderstorms developed across Southwest Arkansas along a residual outflow boundary from convection earlier in the morning. Within an area of slow-moving vorticity, thunderstorms with heavy rainfall rates continued to develop and interact with a very moist and unstable air mass. MLCAPE values across the area were on the order of 1500 to 2500 J/kg, with precipitable water (PW) values of generally ranging between 1.8 to 2.0 inches. Rainfall rates were as high as 2-3 inches per hour, nearing hourly flash flood guidance (FFG) thresholds. Given that these FFG values were quite high, heavy rainfall mainly favored an urban flash flood threat. As a result, only one isolated report of flash flooding was recorded in the city of Texarkana.
episodes.218314: A highly saturated atmosphere coupled with sufficient CAPE produced a significant wet downburst over Morristown during the afternoon hours.
episodes.218338: An upper high near Las Vegas, NV brought weak north to northeast flow over the region.  Drier air at the surface moved in with dew point depressions over 50 degrees.  An upper level disturbance helped thunderstorms develop over area mountains and move into El Paso from the north bringing damaging wind gusts to the city.
episodes.218341: An upper high near Las Vegas, NV brought weak north to northeast flow over the region. Drier air at the surface moved in with dew point depressions over 50 degrees. An upper level disturbance helped thunderstorms develop over the Sacramento Mountains and moved into Otero and Dona Ana counties producing severe wind gusts and dust storms.
episodes.218357: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed across the North Carolina foothills during the late afternoon and evening. One of the storms produced a small area of damaging wind gusts in Catawba County.
episodes.218481: A subtropical high would set up across the central U.S. with troughing off the west coast, setting the stage for a modest monsoonal pattern with storms capable of strong to severe wind gusts.
episodes.218499: A broad area of thunderstorm activity developed during the afternoon of Saturday August 8th.  The region was under deep well mixed conditions with PWAT values greater than 1.6 that allowed for high efficiency precipitation processes.  In addition, strong surface heating created instability and energy.  The final ingredient was a weak mid-level disturbance that tracked across the region.  This allowed multi-cell thunderstorm activity to develop across the state during the afternoon hours.

events.narrative: Multiple videos via social media showed a waterspout produced by a shower just offshore of Folly Beach, SC near the Washout area at 1135 AM. The waterspout moved slowly west-northwest before coming onshore as a tornado at 1136 AM, near the Fort Road and East Ashley Avenue intersection at latitude 32.6704 and longitude -79,9057.

The National Weather Service confirmed an EF0 tornado with an estimated maximum wind speed of 55 mph in Charleston County occurring from 1136 AM to 1137 AM.||Multiple videos via social media showed a waterspout produced by a shower just offshore of Folly Beach, SC near the Washout shifting west-northwest onshore as a tornado at 1136 AM, near the Fort Road and East Ashley Avenue intersection. The tornado then moved across the beach, throwing a few tents/umbrellas, chairs, surfboards and beach coverings into the air before dissipating just beyond East Ashley Avenue approximately 30 seconds after reaching land. Damage was minimal, with only minor impacts seen on video at the beach given a lack of vegetation and structures in the vicinity. Despite the tornado moving directly over a group of people, no injuries have been reported.

An intense thunderstorm produced extensive straight line wind damage across portions of Morristown on Saturday afternoon, August 8th. The first noted damage was minor tree damage along Clearview Road and Central Church Road near Joe Stephens. As the storm collapsed the winds were maximized in a corridor along Central Church Road near Antioch Road, Tennessee Hills Drive, and Grove Dale Drive. Here large swaths of trees were uprooted and blown down primarily to the east and southeast. Some homes sustained moderate to significant damage when trees fell on or through the homes in this area. Preliminary estimates indicated that up to 10 homes may have been damaged in this area. A few power poles were also observed to be snapped or damaged. The maximum estimated winds were also observed in this general location and was estimated to be around 80 mph. The collapsing phase of the storm was finally complete with sporadic tree damage noted on the west side of the country club and near McBride Road and Catron Lane.
